title.en: From the Diary of Anne Frank

text.en: A thirteen-year-old girl begins a diary and names it Kitty. We read some of her early entries.

Anne Frank wrote her diary in Amsterdam during the Second World War. Her first entry says writing in a diary is strange for someone like her.
She says paper has more patience than people and she wants a real friend with whom she can share her feelings.
Although she has loving parents, a sister and about thirty friends, she lacks one true friend to confide in.
So she decides that the diary will be her friend and calls the friend Kitty.
She gives Kitty a short sketch of her life: her father, her mother, her sister Margot and her school.
Her maths teacher Mr Keesing punishes her for talking by giving essay topics such as A Chatterbox and An Incorrigible Chatterbox.
For the third essay, Quack, Quack, Quack, Said Mistress Chatterbox, she writes a clever poem, and the teacher laughs and lets her talk.
The diary shows her honesty and humour. Later the family went into hiding from the Nazis, and the diary became a famous record of those years (background, outside the extract).

problem.en: Anne is 13 and her sister is 16. How many years older is her sister?

why.en: The text says a sixteen-year-old sister.

prompt.en: Why does Anne call her diary Kitty?

requiredIdeas.en: She imagines the friend she longs for

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking Kitty was a real girl

points.en: Anne wrote in Amsterdam during the war.
She wanted a true friend and named the diary Kitty.
Mr Keesing gave her essays on chattering.
Her diary shows honesty and humour.
